subs.l01: In October 2026, the Atlanta Design Festival wrote down why it was losing money.
subs.l02: The explanation is one sentence, halfway down the second page.
subs.l03: Events cost months before they earn a dollar. The time that goes into building them is the time that would go into selling.
subs.l04: This is a reading of that claim, against the festival's own records.
subs.l05: Two internal documents. 18 slides in September. Six in October.
subs.l06: They agree on the numbers. Tour revenue of $14,685, 70% below peak.
subs.l07: Website traffic down a quarter. A mailing list that has not grown. 11 months with no money coming in.
subs.l08: The selling year is thirteen weeks long.
subs.l09: Nine of those weeks produce almost nothing. 10% of the year is in at four weeks out.
subs.l10: 60% arrives in the final week, after every cost has already been paid.
subs.l11: Finding one. The festival cannot forecast, so it cannot commit.
subs.l12: Now the same year, read as a calendar.
subs.l13: Three produced events. A conference, a workshop, and an exhibition. Each takes months of build.
subs.l14: Against that, the selling calendar. Sponsors are approached in Q1. The chapters set budgets in the fall.
subs.l15: Put the two on the same axis.
subs.l17: Finding two. Production does not compete for money. It competes for January, February and March.
subs.l18: Three consequences follow, and none appear in an event budget.
subs.l19: Every product is paid, so nobody who does not already know the festival can enter.
subs.l20: One list, remarketed each year, is the only channel. Flat at about 9,400 names.
subs.l21: And of six things the festival has to sell, two have ever been sold.
subs.l22: Finding three. The loss on the events is the small number. The large one was never worked.
subs.l23: Seattle runs a raw, deliberately unglossy program, and raises five figures from one sponsor.
subs.l24: Portland kept producing. It peaked, and it shut in 2021.
subs.l25: The difference is not production value. It is who does the producing.
subs.l26: What the record establishes, and what it does not.
subs.l27: The festival's own figures were never measured. Nobody has priced the months.
subs.l28: Every source here points at the same place on the calendar. The first quarter.
subs.l29: The decision is whether those months go into building events, or into selling the festival.
